IMPORTANT anti-pattern from this session: when a UI bug looks state/logic-related (e.g. 'scroll position resets'), check whether the real cause is CSS layout timing (elements without fixed dimensions don't have a known size until their content — e.g. a network-fetched image — finishes loading) before assuming it's a JS state-management bug. The first scroll fix (1fb144f) addressed JS state correctly but didn't fix the bug because the actual cause was CSS; the real fix (d6e3606) required giving .photo-card img a fixed width.
